profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting between two workstreams preparing a joint TEMTIA-aligned internal guidance pack for an upcoming multi-site EMT manuscript consortium. The pathology workstream is finalizing image-based annotations from archived tumor sections, while the computational curation workstream is building the shared terminology table and evidence matrix that all sites will use when labeling observations in figures, supplements, and metadata forms. The agenda is to align on the interface between annotated pathology outputs and the shared curation template, confirm what version of the guideline language each team is using, clarify who updates the central term sheet, and agree on what each side will deliver before the consortium's Friday integration checkpoint. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on handoffs: pathology will send 'EMT calls' and example cases, computational curation will fold them into the 'consensus terminology' resource and circulate the consolidated package.

members.name: Dr. Leila Anand
members.expertise: Tumor histopathology, multiplex immunostaining, morphology-based interpretation of epithelial and mesenchymal states
members.background: Leads the tissue-analysis workstream at an academic cancer center and has contributed annotated EMT examples for several multicenter studies, usually working from FFPE sections and pathology review boards.
members.private_state: She wants her team's annotated slide set incorporated without triggering another round of re-review, and she is trying to keep the pathology contribution lightweight because her staff is already committed to another grant deadline.
hidden_assumptions: When the group says 'EMT call,' it means the final specimen-level interpretive label attached to a reviewed case, not marker-by-marker raw observations.
The 'current TEMTIA language' means the wording from the version circulated after last month's editorial comments, even if minor numbering and notes are still being cleaned up.
Uploading examples to the shared terminology resource means sending a frozen PDF and exported image panel to the curation team, who will transpose whatever fields they need.
A case is 'ready for integration' once two pathologists have agreed on the narrative interpretation, even if region-level heterogeneity is only summarized in free text.

members.name: Noah Kim
members.expertise: Ontology mapping, metadata harmonization, cross-study evidence tables, manuscript support for consortium standards
members.background: Coordinates shared data dictionaries and submission templates for a translational research network, with prior work converting narrative biological concepts into structured annotation schemas.
members.private_state: He wants to lock the schema this week so downstream sites stop inventing local labels, and he is worried that any ambiguous pathology input will force manual cleanup across all consortium datasets.
hidden_assumptions: When people say 'EMT call,' they mean the structured annotation package that supports a label, including compartment, marker combination, and evidence code at the region level.
The 'current TEMTIA language' means the v2.1 term sheet in the shared drive that downstream sites are already referencing, regardless of whether some editorial prose changes are pending elsewhere.
Contributions to the shared terminology resource should be entered directly into the live spreadsheet so provenance, synonyms, and cross-references remain intact.
A sample is 'ready for integration' only when its observations can be decomposed into standardized fields without curator interpretation.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that pathology will send over the 'EMT calls' for integration.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means specimen-level interpretive conclusions such as 'partial EMT features present' attached to each reviewed case.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means a structured set of region-level coded observations and supporting evidence fields that justify an EMT-related label.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both routinely use the phrase 'EMT call' as shorthand within their own workstreams, and in a coordination meeting the phrase sounds sufficiently shared that neither expects the other to need the level of granularity spelled out.

misalignment_points.topic: Which 'current TEMTIA language' is in force
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to align everything to the 'current TEMTIA language' or 'latest consensus wording.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the post-editorial draft emailed by the manuscript chair three weeks ago, which adjusted phrasing around 'partial EMT' and moved some cautionary notes into footnotes.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the v2.1 shared-drive term sheet that has stable IDs and synonym columns, but does not yet reflect the chair's latest prose refinements.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both artifacts are recent, both are treated informally as the latest version, and the meeting focuses on coordination rather than explicit document control, so 'latest' feels unambiguous when it is not.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that Leila's cases will be 'ready for integration by Friday.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes readiness means pathology review is complete and each case has a defensible summary label plus representative images.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes readiness means each case can be inserted into the central evidence matrix without additional decomposition, including standardized region identifiers and controlled-vocabulary entries.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In cross-team coordination, 'ready' is a common status word that usually signals schedule confidence rather than a negotiated acceptance criterion, so the latent difference in completeness thresholds stays hidden.

misalignment_points.topic: How updates to the shared term sheet will happen
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that pathology examples and terminology tweaks will be 'added to the sheet' before circulation.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes her team will email annotated PDFs and a comment-marked document, and Noah's team will enter any necessary updates into the live sheet.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes Leila's team will populate designated tabs in the live spreadsheet directly, using locked columns and dropdowns so changes are immediately traceable.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are discussing the same endpoint—information appearing in the sheet—and the mechanics feel like routine administrative detail, making it unlikely either person pauses to verify the exact upload workflow.
